races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Chalice Stakes (Listed Race) (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will shape the entire race; Charlie Johnston's five-year-old has won over 8f on good going and steps back up in trip, but the key question is whether her recent form (11th on return, 4th twice) signals she is short of peak condition at 14d since last run.

runners_data.name: Miss Justice
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's five-year-old has a solid record at 12f on good ground and is a genuine prominent type who can sit just off the leader in an ideal position; the headgear (hood) is noted but she has placed multiple times in similar company and her OR of 101 gives her a strong class case.

runners_data.name: Orchard Keeper
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's mare has an excellent record at 14f, winning and placing multiple times at this trip, and is a proven stayer at the right distance; naturally prominent, she will attempt to take up a forward berth but faces competition for that space, and 296 days off the track is a significant fitness concern on return.

runners_data.name: Orionis
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old is in good hands and showed a win at 12f on good to soft 14 days ago; a true prominent type who will press forward in the early stages despite the map showing midfield, with the slight step up in trip and fast ground being the key unknowns to resolve.

runners_data.name: Revoir
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's four-year-old has posted a string of places without winning in recent starts, suggesting consistent but not dominant form; a genuine prominent type sitting at OR 101, and the visor is noted as a headgear factor, but the lack of a recent win may be a concern at Listed level.

runners_data.name: Ryka
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has won at 12f on soft and good ground and brings solid form at the trip; shown rearward on the map because the field is over-supplied with prominent types, but she is naturally a pace-committed runner and 92 days since last run after a 6th last time raises a fitness flag.

runners_data.name: Gone By
runners_data.note: Lightly weighted three-year-old for Ralph Beckett who has won twice in her last three outings including at 12f on good ground; style is listed as unknown but her progressive profile and trainer's strong recent strike rate make her a notable quantity, especially at 125lbs.

runners_data.name: Romantic Symphony
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's three-year-old won at 11f on a synthetic surface and placed at 12f on good ground; a prominent type with a useful OR of 98 at 125lbs, and the Godolphin handler's 14-day record of 7/20 underlines the yard is in strong form, making her a significant participant.

runners_data.name: Sunshine Star
runners_data.note: John and Thady Gosden's three-year-old has won at 10f on a synthetic surface and placed at 10f on good ground; a natural prominent runner who is stepped up significantly in class and trip today, and with a sim-going record of just 0W1P at true good ground she is yet to fully prove herself on this surface.

races.paceDynamic: Francophone is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of nine and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop over this 1m4f trip on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July Course — a combination that historically rewards horses who can dictate and control tempo without being pressured. Behind her, Miss Justice and Revoir are the likeliest genuine prominent racers to secure the immediate positions, with Romantic Symphony and Gone By likely to track in the early-to-mid group. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions: Orionis, Orchard Keeper, and Sunshine Star are true prominent horses redistributed to midfield on the map, and in practice it is Orionis (William Haggas, strong form, course-appropriate) and Orchard Keeper (Roger Varian, proven at 14f) who are most likely to push forward and actually claim those positions, though doing so will cost them energy. A controlled, single-pacemaker race over a stamina trip on fast ground strongly favours closers with genuine tactical pace or resolute stayers who can produce a sustained run from midfield — horses who travel well in the slipstream and quicken through the final two furlongs will be at the structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Francophone Controls, Challenged Late
scenarios.trigger: If Francophone is allowed to dictate at a steady-to-moderate pace throughout and the field strings out behind her without significant early pressure.
scenarios.body: Francophone sets a comfortable rhythm and the race becomes a stamina-and-class test in the straight, with prominent trackers Miss Justice and Revoir ideally placed to mount a challenge in the final two furlongs; horses travelling well just off the leader's shoulder will be in prime position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Midfield Stalkers Overpower
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest enough to string the field out and redistribute horses from midfield produce a sustained run that overpowers front-runners.
scenarios.body: Gone By, lightly weighted and progressive with a strong recent record, or Romantic Symphony can track into contention and deliver a decisive late challenge as the pace tests every runner's stamina over the final three furlongs.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Crowd the Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Orionis and Orchard Keeper push forward against their mapped positions and create a more pressured early gallop than Francophone anticipates.
scenarios.body: A faster early tempo stretches the field and burns off horses with lower stamina reserves, making this a genuine test of class and fitness; Orionis, if able to hold a prominent berth, and Miss Justice would be best placed to exploit their superior OR and stamina profiles in a more truly-run race.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Finishers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and a sprint finish develops, giving rearward runners a chance to close rapidly.
scenarios.body: Ryka, naturally prominent but mapped rearward, is not a true hold-up type so this scenario lacks an ideal beneficiary; Gone By from an unknown style base is the best-placed candidate if runners do come from off the pace late.

watchPoints.text: Orchard Keeper has been off the track for 296 days — watch her pre-race condition closely, as Roger Varian's mare would need to be fully fit to justify her stayer's profile at Listed level on return.

Orionis, Orchard Keeper, and Sunshine Star are all naturally prominent types who cannot all secure forward positions — watch the early stages for crowding and bumping that could unsettle any of these three runners.

Gone By's running style is listed as unknown and she is a three-year-old stepping into Listed company for the first time — watch how she is ridden in the early furlongs, as her positioning will determine whether she can exploit her light weight.

The going report confirms Good to Firm conditions throughout the card — any horse with a concern about fast ground (note Revoir's soft-ground form figures) should be monitored for any official going change before the off.

Francophone's pace-setting role is central to the entire race shape — if she is taken on early by Orionis or Orchard Keeper pushing forward, the whole tactical dynamic shifts toward Scenario C and the probabilities assigned to Scenario A should be mentally discounted.

races.name: British Stallion Studs Ebf Fillies' Nursery Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Love A Giggle
runners_data.note: Winning form over 5f, now stepping up to 6f on Good-to-Firm, which is a query, but K. R. Burke's yard is firing at 8/36 over 14 days and Clifford Lee is a capable handler of a prominent racer looking to travel just off the pace; the trip extension is the one uncertainty to weigh.

runners_data.name: Acclamation Star
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon in the plate for James Owen (18/50 in form) is a notable booking, but the form reads poorly on this course — a sixth and a tenth over 6f at Goodwood and Newmarket on Good before a win at Ffos Las on Firm; consistency is a concern.

runners_data.name: Glamorize
runners_data.note: George Scott's filly has won twice at 5f on Good and has the highest volume of sim-going experience in this field; steps up to 6f having been beaten 13 lengths at the trip before, so the distance is a live query, and the headgear flag (hg:p) may be a freshener for the extra furlong.

runners_data.name: Havana Sprite
runners_data.note: James Tate's filly arrives on the back of back-to-back wins, both at 5f and 6f on Good, giving her the most rounded recent profile — Good-to-Firm form, proven at the distance, and Jack Mitchell a strong tactical pilot from a prominent position.

runners_data.name: Rollthedicebaby
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon has 12 winners from 59 runners over 14 days; this filly is a genuine prominent racer by nature but the field's depth of pace means she is likely to find herself shuffled back, and the redistribution note should temper confidence — her chance is real if she can recover her natural position but that is not guaranteed.

runners_data.name: Lady Dublin
runners_data.note: Ollie Pears's filly has won her last two starts over 6f at this exact course on Good, making her the standout course-and-distance specialist at the front; only 8 days since her last run, which is worth monitoring, but her confirmed lead-making style gives her first call on a clean break.

runners_data.name: Donegal Rose
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's filly brings a 6f win on Good to the table and will be pressing for the early lead alongside Lady Dublin; she ran too freely when stepped to 7f last time and the drop back to 6f is a clear positive, though winning this contested duel from OR 72 is a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Fire Thunder
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's filly has been consistently placed, including a win over this course and distance on Good, and her ability to travel up with the pace is genuine — however, the volume of prominent types in this field means she is most likely to be bumped back from her natural position, and that style displacement is a real check on her prospects.

runners_data.name: Holi Scarlett
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's filly has a win at 5f on Good and has placed three times in six recorded runs; she is a natural front-to-prominent runner by inclination, yet with six prominent types all wanting forward positions she is among the least likely to secure that ground, and Olivia Haines's 7lb claim does not offset that positional disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Lady Dublin and Donegal Rose are confirmed front-runners and will fight for the early lead from the gates on this straight Newmarket 6f, generating an honest, pressured gallop that is unlikely to relent on ground riding Good to Firm. Four of nine runners want prominent positions — Love A Giggle, Acclamation Star, Glamorize, and Havana Sprite will all be angling forward early, creating a congested 2-3 furlong stretch where traffic interference is a real risk for those who can't secure the rail. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Fire Thunder and Holi Scarlett are natural prominent racers who are most unlikely to get into their preferred position and will be shuffled back under pressure from better-drawn or faster-away rivals. This contested, end-to-end gallop on fast ground over a straight sprint track strongly favours exposed, prominent-to-leading types with proven Good-to-Firm form who can travel prominently without covering extra ground — horses who can lock in a handy position early and sustain it, rather than closers who must navigate traffic from an unnatural position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Hold Sway
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is honest but not suicidal and the prominent horses lock in their positions cleanly by the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: Love A Giggle, Glamorize, and Havana Sprite — all with strong Good-to-Firm form — sit just off the two leaders and sweep past in the final furlong as the pace-setters crack; Newmarket's straight track rewards those who travel prominently and sustain their run without checking.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Lady Dublin or Donegal Rose gains a clean break and the contested pace actually strings the field out, leaving no challenger with a clean run.
scenarios.body: One of the two pace-setters — most likely Lady Dublin given her back-to-back 6f wins at this track on Good — kicks clear at the 2f pole and the prominent pack are too busy fighting each other to close; a flat, fast Newmarket straight with minimal bend favours a horse who can sustain its lead when the ground rides quick.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Traffic Carnage, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent logjam 2-3 out causes interference and choppy runs, allowing a horse to thread through late.
scenarios.body: The congested middle-race scrimmage creates gaps in the final furlong that a horse finishing from slightly off the pace can exploit, but this scenario is materially discounted because the true hold-up types in this field are actually prominent racers redistributed to the rear — they are not natural closers.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, All Tire
scenarios.trigger: If both front-runners burn each other out too quickly and the entire prominent group weakens in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: An unusually strong early duel between Lady Dublin and Donegal Rose drains the field, and a horse who managed to switch off slightly and is handed a soft lead into the final furlong benefits — but this is the least likely shape given Newmarket's straight configuration rewards even-tempo galloping rather than producing dramatic late surges.

watchPoints.text: Lady Dublin and Donegal Rose will fight for the lead from the gates — watch for a fierce battle in the opening furlong that could either string the field out cleanly or burn both leaders off before halfway.

The four-way prominent cluster of Love A Giggle, Acclamation Star, Glamorize, and Havana Sprite creates a congestion flashpoint 2-3 furlongs out — any horse forced to check or switch could lose the race there and then on a track with no bend to recover.

Fire Thunder and Holi Scarlett are natural prominent types mapped to midfield by redistribution — watch at the start to see whether either can hustle forward; if they can, the pace dynamic becomes even more pressured and the front-runners are more exposed.

Glamorize's headgear flag (first-time hood/piece noted) is worth monitoring in the paddock — if it sharpens her early, she could be more prominent than expected and add further to the pace congestion.

Good-to-Firm is the verified going for the 2:13 slot per the going report, despite the race card listing Good — horses without proven Good-to-Firm form, or those with a going concern flag, should be discounted accordingly.

races.name: Lodge At The National Stud Ebf Fillies' Novice Stakes (gbb Race)
Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Saxony
runners_data.note: Confirmed pace-setter with a recent course win over this exact 7f on good ground; even as a hold from the front the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence if unable to fully dictate — his sim-going strike rate is modest (0W2P at 7f good), but today's uncontested role is his best chance.

runners_data.name: Hardy's Hero
runners_data.note: William Haggas three-year-old with an excellent consistent form profile (2W6P in similar going), but his natural instinct to race prominently means he is liable to find himself racing wider and further back than ideal; watch for Cieren Fallon managing the early fractions carefully.

runners_data.name: Lion Of Mali
runners_data.note: In strong current form (1-2-1 in last three starts), this James Fanshawe three-year-old wants to bowl along in front, and being forced to track against instinct on fast ground at Newmarket is a real positional headache that Jack Mitchell will need to navigate.

runners_data.name: Electrical
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for Brian Toomey, though recent form figures of 8-4-7-6-7 make enthusiasm difficult; the step up from a 12f experiment back to 7f removes the stamina concern but the flat track and fast surface expose a lack of class at this OR.

runners_data.name: Tryst
runners_data.note: Arrived here with a 7f Newmarket win already on the card (last start, good ground) and Billy Loughnane's positional awareness is a real asset; rated the highest in the field at OR 87 and the headgear note (hg:p) suggests a sharper professional approach — a horse that profiles well for the dominant race shape.

runners_data.name: Sierra Sands
runners_data.note: Two wins from last three starts, both over 6f-7f on good ground at this course, giving him the strongest course-and-distance profile in the field; Robert Havlin knows this track intimately and a stalking role behind Spirit Of Saxony maps directly onto what he has done to win here before.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Of Saxony is the lone confirmed front runner and, with only Sierra Sands likely to contest early prominence alongside Hardy's Hero and Lion Of Mali pressing from behind, the pace should be honest but controlled — Spirit Of Saxony can dictate a measured gallop down the Newmarket July course straight without being seriously harassed. The field contains more natural prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Hardy's Hero and Lion Of Mali are genuine front-rank horses who will likely find themselves shuffled into a midfield berth against their instincts, creating a degree of positional friction in the first two furlongs. Sierra Sands has the gate speed and recent course-winning form to slot in just behind Spirit Of Saxony and race in a perfect stalking position throughout. This race shape — a single unhurried pace-setter, a fast surface, and genuine prominent types forced to track — strongly favours the close-order stalker who can travel sweetly in second or third and pounce inside the final furlong without needing to make up ground from deep.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stalker Pounces Off Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Saxony sets an uncontested, sustainable tempo and the race is decided by which horse travels best in second or third before kicking.
scenarios.body: Spirit Of Saxony's moderate gallop sets the race up as a waiting game for horses travelling in his slipstream, with the winner emerging from a position just off the pace in the straight; the fast going rewards smooth, economical racing rather than late acceleration from deep.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Helps Late Closer
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Of Saxony goes too hard early despite being uncontested and ties up inside the final two furlongs, gifting the finish to a hold-up horse.
scenarios.body: An honest early tempo on fast ground can still stretch the field if the front runner misjudges effort, leaving a gap for a finisher from off the pace; the short straight at Newmarket July makes this scenario less likely but not impossible.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scramble Quickens Pace
scenarios.trigger: If Hardy's Hero or Lion Of Mali refuse to settle behind Spirit Of Saxony and push up to contest the lead, lifting the pace materially.
scenarios.body: Both horses being out of their natural position creates risk of a messy, quicker-than-expected early fractions as they seek to recover lost ground; a stronger gallop would compress the field and could bring the most versatile runner into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Draw Or Traffic Decides
scenarios.trigger: If positional disadvantage or traffic in a compressed field results in one horse being severely compromised regardless of running style.
scenarios.body: With six runners on a flat, straight track the draw and early positioning matter less than in bigger fields, but a horse losing its rhythm at the start or getting boxed in could be decisive; the winner in this scenario is whoever avoids interference and has the clearest run.

watchPoints.text: Sierra Sands and Spirit Of Saxony — watch the split between them at the two-furlong pole; if Sierra Sands is within a length travelling easily, he is in a race-winning position and the gap may not narrow.

Hardy's Hero and Lion Of Mali — both will instinctively push forward from the gates; if either overcomes the redistribution and secures a prominent berth, the effective pace increases and Scenario A becomes less clean.

Tryst — dropping back from 10f to 7f after soft-ground struggles, returning to winning conditions (7f, good, Newmarket); his OR 87 top weight makes him the class reference, and Billy Loughnane's positioning in the first furlong will be telling.

Electrical — Brian Toomey's 0/1 14-day strike rate and Electrical's string of poor finishes suggest this runner is unlikely to factor unless the race falls completely apart; a non-trivial price may tempt, but the form wall is real.

Going clarification — declared as Good but the course going report consistently shows Good to Firm across all races today including both 7f slots; expect fast-ground conditions that reward economical racing over raw stamina.

races.name: Racing Welfare Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Haku
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who has placed at 1m2f–1m4f on Flat AW mostly; Mark Loughnane runner returning from 185 days off — fitness a genuine question, but Charles Bishop rides and the horse's prominent style suits the likely race shape if fitness is there.|

runners_data.name: Way Of Life
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old with three wins from five efforts at up to 1m1f on turf, ridden by claimer Olivia Tubb (5lb); sole confirmed pace-setter who will have this race to himself up front, but sim-going record reads just 0 wins from 4 placed attempts on going softer than firm, and the STYLE_FIT tag signals he is racing out of role by being classified prominent rather than as the leader he truly is — his chance is real if he controls matters, fragile if opposed.|

runners_data.name: Sixpack
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners this six-year-old who has won twice at 1m4f–1m6f including on good ground, with a peak run fourth at 2m; a genuine hold-up performer wearing a hood, his sim-going record of 2 wins and 4 places from 6 gives him solid claims if the pace quickens enough to bring him into it late.|

runners_data.name: Arqoob
runners_data.note: Lucy Wadham's eight-year-old carries a hood and has placed three times at 1m4f–1m5f on good ground in recent starts; consistent enough but a 0-for-last-many run of form and a trainer with no wins in the last 14 days tempers expectations, though his proximity to the pace keeps him in the frame.|

runners_data.name: Greek Order
runners_data.note: Michael Bell gelding stepping up in trip from recent 1m efforts where he has finished no better than fourth in five straight; the field's positional crowding means he is unlikely to find his natural prominent slot, and with a STYLE_FIT discount and poor recent form, his chance in this shape is limited.|

runners_data.name: Divine Knight
runners_data.note: William Haggas five-year-old with two placed efforts at 1m4f including on good ground, partnered by Cieren Fallon — the strongest jockey-trainer combination among the displaced prominent types; though the redistribution means he may race further back than ideal, his trip form is the most directly relevant of the three bumped runners.|

runners_data.name: Almekarem
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's lightly raced four-year-old won on good ground over 1m just 10 days ago, so freshness is not a concern; stepping up sharply in trip to 1m4f is the key question, and his hold-up profile means he needs the pace to quicken to bring him into calculations.|

runners_data.name: First Officer
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam's seven-year-old has finished second twice and third twice at 1m2f–1m4f on good-ish ground in recent starts — solid consistency — but the apprentice rider (7lb) and his displacement to midfield from his natural prominent berth mean he may struggle to replicate those front-rank efforts from further back.|

races.paceDynamic: Way Of Life is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine rival to press him through the early stages, he is likely to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f on Good to Firm ground. Haku and Arqoob are the natural prominent companions who will track him into the race, but neither has the profile to force a genuinely searching tempo, meaning the pace is likely to be honest rather than fierce. The redistribution flags on Greek Order, Divine Knight, and First Officer signal that this field carries more prominent-minded types than the race shape can accommodate — of those three, Divine Knight (recent 1m4f form) and Greek Order (likely to try to slot in early) are the most likely to secure a forward berth, while First Officer risks being shuffled wider and back. With a controlled tempo set by a single leader and no genuine hold-up specialist bar Sixpack and Almekarem, this race shape most strongly favours prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can travel sweetly close to the pace and produce a sustained, rather than explosive, finishing effort.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stalkers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Way Of Life dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race is only truly run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Way Of Life sets a steady tempo that compresses the field and rewards horses travelling economically just off the pace; those sitting second or third can produce a sustained challenge without needing a sharp turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On, Front Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Way Of Life's moderate fractions prove genuinely slow enough that he preserves enough to last home on good to firm ground.
scenarios.body: An uncontested leader on quick ground who has already demonstrated he can win at this trip from the front simply extends his advantage turning in; horses tracking him lack the sprint to close.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Overhaul Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is quicker than expected and the leaders are run off their legs in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Sixpack, a genuine hold-up performer with two wins at this trip and strong form on good ground, would be ideally placed to reel them in; Almekarem, fresh off a recent win, could also finish with purpose from off the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Scrappy Moderate Renewal
scenarios.trigger: If the redistribution causes early positional friction, bunching the prominent types and producing an uneven, muddling tempo.
scenarios.body: Disrupted early order unsettles horses whose natural style has been displaced; Arqoob, the most experienced here at this trip on good ground, may benefit from the chaos if he threads through late.

watchPoints.text: Way Of Life's claimer Olivia Tubb (5lb) controls the pace entirely — if she goes too steady, the race telescopes and prominent stalkers like Haku and Divine Knight have a simple task; watch the early fractions for the tempo he sets.|

Greek Order, Divine Knight, and First Officer all want to race prominently but cannot all do so — early jostling for position between these three in the first furlong could disrupt the field and compromise all three runners' chances.|

Sixpack is the only horse in the field with proven form at 2m, suggesting he will finish strongly if the pace is genuine, but on a steady gallop his hold-up style may leave him with too much ground to make up over 1m4f.|

Almekarem's trip jump from 1m to 1m4f on just his sixth career start is the most significant unknown in the race; Prescott is expert at placing horses, but the extra four furlongs on quick ground is unproven territory.|

The going is officially Good but every race on the card has been run on Good to Firm — conditions are faster than the declared going and will suit horses with turf form on quicker surfaces; check Sixpack and Divine Knight's firm-ground credentials most closely.|

races.name: National Stud Fillies' Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Food For Thought
runners_data.note: Uncontested front-runner for Ralph Beckett who has won and placed over 10f on Good ground — stepping up to 1m2f suits her stamina profile, and with no pressure expected, she can control the pace, though four rivals matching or bettering her on the day remains the risk at OR 82.

runners_data.name: Thaluna
runners_data.note: William Haggas runner who has finished second and third at 7-8f on Good ground with Cieren Fallon likely to have her travelling prominently — she has placed in five of six Good-ground starts and stepping up to 1m2f looks a logical progression from her 8f efforts.

runners_data.name: Hollywell Stream
runners_data.note: Jane Chapple-Hyam filly who naturally settles at the rear, with a placed effort over 10f on Good ground in her favour, but in a four-runner field with a controlled front-runner, the hold-up position is structurally compromised and she needs more pace than Food For Thought is likely to generate.

runners_data.name: Valkyrie Storm
runners_data.note: Has won twice over 8f on Good going and drops back in weights to OR 75, giving Eve Johnson Houghton's filly a potential edge — she was prominent when winning and that style translates well to this shape, though the step to 1m2f with only two runs at the trip is the key unknown.

races.paceDynamic: Food For Thought is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of just four, and with no rival likely to contest her for the lead, she will bowl along at a controlled, sustainable tempo on the Newmarket July Course straight. Thaluna and Valkyrie Storm will both track up prominently behind her, creating a compressed three-horse group early, while Hollywell Stream drops in at the rear under Billy Loughnane. With Good To Firm conditions rewarding horses who travel fluently and maintain their gallop rather than those requiring a strong pace injection, the shape of this race heavily favours prominent racers who can sit close to a comfortable lead and pounce at the two-furlong pole. Hold-up horses are at a structural disadvantage here — the tempo will not be fast enough to force the leaders to capitulate, meaning the race is likely won from on or near the front.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Food For Thought dictates a measured pace and the prominent pair Thaluna and Valkyrie Storm engage at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Food For Thought's uncontested lead sets a rhythm that suits horses travelling on the bridle in second and third, and as the race quickens in the final two furlongs, Thaluna and Valkyrie Storm have the positional advantage to attack. Cieren Fallon's race management on Thaluna and the consistent Newmarket form of both prominent runners make this the dominant shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Food For Thought finds a truly sustainable rhythm and the pace is slow enough that she simply never gets caught.
scenarios.body: At Newmarket's July Course over 1m2f with only four runners, a front-runner can at times dictate so effectively that chasers are unable to accelerate past, particularly if the early tempo is deceptive and rivals leave the winning move too late. Food For Thought has winning form over 10f on Good going and Ralph Beckett's yard is in form, giving this a credible if secondary probability.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong early and Hollywell Stream's hold-up position turns into a genuine advantage in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Hollywell Stream has placed at 10f on Good ground before and Billy Loughnane may track wide to find a clear run, but in a four-runner field with no guaranteed strong pace, the margins needed for a late closer to overhaul a prominent field rarely materialise. This scenario requires a pace scenario contrary to what Food For Thought's solo-lead profile generates.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset, Wide Open Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the field fails to cohere tactically and multiple horses hit the front simultaneously in a scrambled finish.
scenarios.body: With only four runners and clear positional hierarchy, a chaotic conclusion is the least likely outcome, and only applies if jockeys radically misread the pace or a horse suffers interference. The low probability reflects that this race has a well-defined structure, not a chaotic multi-pace battle.

watchPoints.text: Food For Thought sets the pace from the front entirely unchallenged — if she finds a deeply comfortable rhythm, Thaluna and Valkyrie Storm must decide early whether to close or risk giving her too much rope, and a miscalculation could let her slip the field.

Valkyrie Storm is 12 days since her last run and has been freshened quickly — monitor how she settles early, as a keen or unbalanced showing at the start of 1m2f on a track she is unproven at could undermine her chance despite the attractive OR drop.

Hollywell Stream's hold-up position in a four-runner field with a controlled pace is a structural trap — Billy Loughnane will need to make a very early decision about whether to move earlier than the horse's natural style dictates or accept a likely closing deficit.

Good To Firm conditions are faster than the nominal Good stated for the race — all four runners have Good-ground form, but pace on Fast turf at Newmarket can compress the finishing furlong, slightly benefiting those who are already positioned close to the leader rather than those running into the bridle from off the pace.

races.name: British Racing School Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner for Stuart Williams, carrying the tongue tie and hood combination; five-day turnaround is quick but the horse has placed twice over five furlongs on Good ground recently with similar-going form showing one win and five places from 15 runs — likely to need things to go wrong up front to get involved.

runners_data.name: Silky Robin
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Good ground over five and six furlongs give Brian Toomey's runner obvious each-way claims; the 40-day absence is the main query, but the horse has shown it can handle a break and Joe Leavy's booking adds confidence — the prominent style is perfectly suited to tracking Sound And Vision before challenging late.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Point
runners_data.note: Adam Kirby trains but William Carson rides this hold-up type who has placed twice over five furlongs on Good ground; the tongue tie and cheekpiece combination suggests some headgear reliance, and a run 15 days ago over the same trip means the horse is fit — but a form figure of 0 on last outing at this trip on Good ground is a concern.

runners_data.name: Sound And Vision
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's three-year-old is the lone confirmed front-runner and a low STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) indicates it may not be operating entirely to type in this shape; Billy Loughnane's booking is a positive, and one win from six on similar going is modest, but the ability to dictate unchallenged is a significant structural advantage in this six-runner race on a flat, straight sprint.

runners_data.name: Dottie Diamond
runners_data.note: William Stone's four-year-old arrives on the back of three wins from four runs including two on Good ground over five furlongs — the form is excellent; however, the horse's natural hold-up style means it has been pushed into a midfield mapping here because the rear is overcrowded with similar types, and Jack Mitchell will need to find a way through in the final two furlongs rather than operating from its preferred position.

runners_data.name: Angel Summer
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon takes over for Patrick Owens on this three-year-old who is a natural hold-up type similarly displaced from the rear in the pace mapping; a five-day turnaround is fine for freshness but the horse has no wins and no places on similar going from seven attempts, and the move up from lower-grade form makes this a tough assignment even before accounting for the positional challenge.

races.paceDynamic: Sound And Vision is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with just six runners on Newmarket's July Course five-furlong straight, faces no meaningful rival for the lead — Billy Loughnane can dictate an entirely sustainable gallop without being pressed. The going report confirms Good To Firm conditions for this race, which rewards early momentum and horses that can be delivered into a position off a controlled pace rather than having to lunge from deep. Silky Robin is the only other prominent-style runner and is most likely to track Sound And Vision in second, but with no pressure coming at the leader the pace will be metronomic and honest rather than brutally fast. This shape — a lone front-runner setting a controlled tempo — classically suits prominent-to-midfield runners who can sit in behind, conserve energy over the first furlong and pounce in the final two; the field holds more hold-up types than can realistically operate from the rear, with Dottie Diamond and Angel Summer both true hold-up horses who have been redistributed to map midfield, meaning Silky Robin, tracking close to the pace, is best placed to exploit the shape if Sound And Vision ties up.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Rails Run
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision dictates a sustainable pace unchallenged and the field is stretched over the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Sound And Vision sets the fractions from the front with Loughnane sitting chilly, and a prominent stalker travelling smoothly can pick them up inside the final furlong without needing to come from an impossible position; Good To Firm ground rewards those who travel into the race rather than making up ground from rear.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Silky Robin travels fluidly in Sound And Vision's slipstream and quickens past them inside the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Silky Robin has won twice in similar conditions over five and six furlongs on Good ground and carries the profile of a horse that has been freshened (40 days since last run) and is returning in form after back-to-back wins; if Sound And Vision's controlled pace gives way under pressure, Silky Robin's recent winning momentum makes them the most obvious beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sharply mid-race, stringing the field out and leaving a gap for a late finisher.
scenarios.body: Dottie Diamond has a strong recent record (three wins from four runs) and on fast ground over five furlongs a sprint-finish could materialise if the pace hots up; however, being a true hold-up horse mapped to midfield due to redistribution, getting into a winning position from behind on this tight, flat sprint is a significant ask against a controlled gallop.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Wide Finish
scenarios.trigger: If Sound And Vision is outrun or fails to sustain the gallop and the race becomes a scramble in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: In a messy finish where the front-runners come back to the field, a horse like Merrimack — who has placed twice over five furlongs on Good ground and is dropped back in trip — could emerge from the pack; Angel Summer is out of depth at this level on current form and would need the race to fall apart entirely, making this the least likely shape.

watchPoints.text: Sound And Vision — if Billy Loughnane gets a completely uncontested lead at a controlled tempo, this horse becomes structurally very hard to peg back in a six-runner sprint despite modest similar-going form.

Silky Robin — watch whether Joe Leavy gets the horse tucked in directly behind Sound And Vision early; if Silky Robin is caught three or four wide at the head of the pack, the energy cost over five furlongs on Good To Firm ground becomes significant.

Dottie Diamond — despite the strongest recent form in the race (three wins from four), Jack Mitchell will need a slice of luck to find daylight in the final two furlongs given the horse is not operating from its natural position and the pace is unlikely to collapse.

Angel Summer — monitor market moves closer to post; the horse has no placed form on similar going and steps up in class, but Cieren Fallon's booking in a small field means any drifting in the ring would be informative about stable confidence.

Tuscan Point — the combination of cheekpieces and tongue tie flags a horse that can be tricky to assess; any slow early pace that removes the need to hold a prominent position could see Tuscan Point emerge more prominently than the recent form string suggests.
